solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beautiful woman in New York taking speed?

indicators.note: New York taking speed means the city's letters are followed by the speed's letters

parts.note: speed is measured in mph, miles per hour

explanation.surface: A lovely woman in Manhattan seems to be on drugs, speed being slang for amphetamine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'speed' is not the drug but a unit of velocity.
explanation.definitionFit: In mythology and poetic usage a beautiful young woman is likened to the nature spirits of Greek legend.

clue.text: Noble opposed old king initially in secluded place

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A nobleman who opposed an ageing monarch seems to have retreated somewhere hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A small corner tucked away from view is a sheltered, secluded spot.

clue.text: Nearly all Medical Officer's time

parts.note: MO is the abbreviation for Medical Officer, plus the 's

explanation.surface: Almost all of an army doctor's hours, it seems, are taken up.
explanation.definitionFit: The greater part of something, the majority, is nearly the whole of it.

clue.text: Where recluse lives — male in tradition passed down

indicators.note: in tells us the male's letter goes inside the word for tradition

parts.note: heritage is the tradition handed down through generations

explanation.surface: A hermit's home is described in terms of men and inherited customs.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded dwelling for someone living alone in religious retreat is named after the hermit who occupies it.

clue.text: Jack in Police Department is commended

indicators.note: in says the word for jack sits inside the police abbreviation

parts.note: to jack something up is to raise it

explanation.surface: A man called Jack serving in the police force has received a commendation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name, but it is the verb, as when lifting a car with a jack.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend someone is to speak highly of them, a synonym for lauding them.

clue.text: Fish pies seen around South Carolina

indicators.note: around says the word pies is wrapped about the state's abbreviation

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for the US state of South Carolina

explanation.surface: Fish pies have been spotted in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish pies' reads as a dish, but 'Fish' alone is the definition and 'pies' is taken literally as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign of the twelfth house is represented by a pair of fish, and is often simply called the Fish.

clue.text: Suitable physical training after first of August

indicators.note: after says the training abbreviation comes after the August letter
first of means only the opening letter of August is used

explanation.surface: Exercise classes are deemed appropriate once August begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suitable is fitting or appropriate for the purpose.

clue.text: Saw ankle moving in ballet

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the two words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone noticed an ankle in motion during a ballet performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's famous ballet about Odette, the enchanted swan princess, is an example of the genre.

clue.text: More dismal, stop working clutching back? Right

indicators.note: clutching says the word for stop working holds the word for back inside it

parts.note: a machine that stops working is said to die
the rear is the back of something

explanation.surface: Someone finds things grimmer as they quit work while gripping a sore back.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of dreary: gloomier, bleaker, and more depressing than before.

clue.text: Inferior old strongholds, small inside

indicators.note: inside says the letter for small goes within the word for strongholds

parts.note: forts are fortified strongholds
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Ancient castles are dismissed as second-rate, each with a tiny room inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described with this phrase is barely deserving of the name, mediocre or poor quality.

clue.text: In Perth an esteemed title, once

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A respected historic rank is mentioned in connection with the Scottish city of Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth is a city in Scotland, fitting the Scottish rank, as in Shakespeare's Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Scottish rank of nobility, held by a clan chief or lord, now historical.

clue.text: After victory English trader, we hear, goes here for drinks?

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for trader is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a seller is someone who trades goods

explanation.surface: A merchant celebrates a win by heading somewhere for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottles of wine are stored in an underground room, so that is where they are placed.

clue.text: Environmental refusal supported by film magazine

indicators.note: in a down clue the film word sits below and so props up the earlier pieces

parts.note: eco- is the prefix for environmental, as in eco-friendly
no is a refusal
a film is a thin coating such as a mist

explanation.surface: A green group's rejection is backed by a cinema journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests cinema, but here it is a thin haze.
explanation.definitionFit: The British weekly current affairs and business periodical bears this name.

clue.text: Not knowing inn argot, confused

indicators.note: confused says the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled by the slang used in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or awareness of something means being uninformed about it.

clue.text: More about origins of that good and generous loan

indicators.note: about says the word More goes round the letters that follow
origins of tells us to take the first letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A loan is described as more than good and generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A home loan secured against property is the commonest kind of borrowing for a house.

clue.text: Shot girl receives known the world over

indicators.note: receives says the word for girl takes the word for shot inside it

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a lob is a high shot in tennis

explanation.surface: A girl who was shot is now famous worldwide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as a past participle, but it is a noun, the tennis stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worldwide in reach is recognised internationally, across every country.

clue.text: Chesspiece that is used by new recruit

parts.note: the rook is the chess piece also called the castle
ie is the abbreviation for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A beginner is given a chess piece to use.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or newcomer, especially in a sports team or the police, is a raw beginner.

clue.text: Spoils hay at edges, likely to get wet

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it

indicators.note: at edges tells us to take only the first and last letters of hay

explanation.surface: Rain ruins hay stacked at the field margins, which are prone to flooding.
explanation.definitionFit: Boggy, waterlogged ground is soggy and liable to be soaked.

clue.text: Oonagh went for reform, avoiding alcohol

indicators.note: reform says the letters of the two words are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman named Oonagh went in for self-improvement by giving up drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from the water wagon: someone on it drinks only water.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom describes a person who has sworn off drink and is staying teetotal.

clue.text: Pressure over spat in part of boat

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the pressure letter above the quarrel word

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
a spat is a quarrel, a row

explanation.surface: Tension over a quarrel aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The front end of a vessel, its bow, is one section of the hull.

clue.text: Fight playfully with Pole

definitions.meaning: boxers practise by sparring, fighting without real intent
a stout pole used for a ship's mast or boom

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to box in practice and a ship's pole, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Some trial, a month in siege site

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a month-long trial is held at the site of a famous siege.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texas mission besieged by Mexican forces in 1836 is a famous battle site.

clue.text: Strange, like one or three

definitions.meaning: one and three are numbers not divisible by two

explanation.definitionFit: The word means peculiar, and also describes whole numbers that leave a remainder when halved.

clue.text: Purr — it's over rider's equipment

indicators.note: over says the letters of the first two words are turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: A cat's contented sound is over, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The foot support hanging from a saddle is part of a horse rider's tack.

clue.text: Sea duty arranged — twenty-four hours

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor's shift at sea has been scheduled for a whole day.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekday, like any day of the week, lasts a full day and night.

clue.text: Building we found in shelter of hill

indicators.note: the word we is found sheltered inside the word for hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Some people have discovered a building on a hillside refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall structure such as a castle keep or church spire is a kind of building.
